articles.headlineTranslated: Fukuoka City forms Infectious Disease Crisis Management Expert Committee; measles outbreak, hantavirus outbreak, affecting 20 healthcare workers.
articles.summary: Fukuoka City forms Infectious Disease Crisis Management Expert Committee as nationwide measles outbreaks and hantavirus detected on an Atlantic Ocean cruise ship raise concerns. The gathering aligns with concerns over measles activity nationwide and a hantavirus case on an Atlantic cruise ship. On May 25, about 20 healthcare professionals gathered at Fukuoka City Hall to discuss emergency coordination and strengthen information sharing for potential contingencies. Proceedings were closed to the press. This year, nationwide measles cumulative cases reached 479 as of May 13. The meeting underscores local readiness to respond to overseas-origin infectious disease events, with emphasis on inter-agency collaboration and rapid information exchange to prevent and manage outbreaks.

articles.headlineTranslated: In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccine hesitancy? ... Measles vaccination rate has fallen; Fukui Prefecture says "the most effective preventive measure to curb the spread of infection" | Medical | News from Fukui | Fukui Shimbun ONLINE
articles.summary: Measles vaccination rates in Fukui Prefecture have fallen below the 95% herd-immunity target, with two-dose MR (measles-rubella) vaccination administered at ages 12–24 months and before entering elementary school (5–7). In 2024, first-dose coverage was 92.6% and second-dose 92.4%; earlier years saw declines (2022 second dose 92.1%; 2023 and 2024 slipping below 95% for the first or second dose). National measles cases reached 479 as of May 13, 2026, the second-highest pace in the past decade after 2019; Fukui has recorded one infection last year and one this year. A 40-year-old man in Fukui contracted measles after traveling to Vietnam in late April. Measles is highly infectious via airborne, droplet, and contact transmission; incubation about 10 days; symptoms start with fever and cough, then high fever and rash, with pneumonia or otitis media risk. Vaccination reduces disease risk and severity.

articles.headlineTranslated: SEVENTEEN confirms measles cases among attendees of the Tokyo Dome fan meeting; warning issued: "To everyone who attended the relevant performance."
articles.summary: Measles cases have been reported among attendees of SEVENTEEN's Tokyo Dome show on May 13, 2026, prompting an updated warning from the group’s official site on May 22. The notice states that some concert-goers were subsequently diagnosed with measles (Rubeola); no specific case count is provided. Measles is described as an acute, highly contagious viral infection transmitted via airborne, droplet, and contact routes, with nearly 100% attack rate in non-immune individuals and lifelong immunity after infection. Symptoms typically emerge about 10 days after exposure, including fever, cough, runny nose, and conjunctivitis; after 2–3 days of fever, high fever (>39°C) and a rash develop. Attendees with suspected symptoms are urged to contact a medical facility in advance before seeking care. Health authorities will maintain safety measures under governmental guidance to ensure safe future performances.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles Surge Traced to Imported Cases, but Questions Remain on Maintaining Elimination Status.
articles.summary: Measles in Japan surged in 2026, concentrated in the Kanto, Chubu, and Kansai regions, with 479 provisional cases reported in Week 19 (May 4–10) and year-to-date totals already surpassing the 2025 annual figure of 265. Health authorities warn that imported cases appear to have sparked the domestic outbreak, raising questions about how Japan can sustain its measles elimination status. The article quotes Sayaka Takanashi, head of the Vaccination Research Division at the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, who discusses epidemiological trends both domestic and international, and notes that the first installment examines epidemiology while the second will address the role and strategies of measles vaccination. The data indicate ongoing transmission and the need for vigilant surveillance, vaccination coverage, and import-related controls to prevent setback of elimination goals.

The article quotes Sayaka Takanashi, head of the Vaccination Research Division at the National Institute of Infectious Diseases, who discusses epidemiological trends both domestic and international, and notes that the first installment examines epidemiology while the second will address the role and strategies of measles vaccination. The data indicate ongoing transmission and the need for vigilant surveillance, vaccination coverage, and import-related controls to prevent setback of elimination goals.

articles.headlineTranslated: Editorial: Do not underestimate measles; prevent its spread.
articles.summary: Measles infections are rising in Japan, with 479 cases by May 10, 2026, near the highest level since elimination was declared. Measles is highly contagious and spreads airborne; the 10–12 day incubation produces fever ≥39°C, cough, runny nose, and rash. In pregnancy, there is a risk of miscarriage or preterm birth; rare but severe outcomes include acute encephalitis and death. Vaccination remains the only effective preventive measure. Japan’s routine immunization began in 1978, with two doses since 2006; two-dose immunity or prior infection generally provides protection. Current outbreaks are largely import-driven; global waves and pandemic-era declines in vaccination increased susceptibility. Two-dose coverage was 91% in FY2024, below the 95% target. In Tokyo, free vaccination for exposed individuals began on the 18th; authorities may expand public vaccination access for healthcare workers, school staff, and travelers to curb spread.

articles.headlineTranslated: Five Key Points to Know in Measles Management: 2026 Revised Edition
articles.summary: Measles in Japan continues into 2026, with school-based clusters reported in Aichi Prefecture, Kagoshima Prefecture, and Tokyo. Many cases lack a clear transmission source, increasing vigilance for healthcare facilities about when a measles suspect might present. Keiko Taya of the Kanagawa Prefectural Institute of Public Health outlines five key points for measles management in the revised 2026 edition: (1) early recognition of measles signs in patients presenting to clinics and hospitals, (2) prompt laboratory confirmation, (3) immediate infection control measures to prevent nosocomial spread, (4) rapid public health notification and contact tracing, (5) vaccination considerations for patients and contacts and evaluation of exposure. The update emphasizes ongoing local transmission in addition to imported cases and underscores the need for preparedness in schools and medical settings.

articles.headlineTranslated: Tokyo to offer free measles vaccines to contacts of measles cases at eight sites in Tokyo from the 18th.
articles.summary: Tokyo will launch emergency measles vaccination for close contacts of measles patients, offering free MR (measles-rubella) vaccines at eight designated infectious-disease medical institutions from May 18, 2026. Targeting residents who had contact within 72 hours with a measles patient, have not had confirmed infection, and have received only one vaccine dose. Public health centers will identify contacts from patient travel and exposure histories and vaccinate with consent. As of May 14, 2026, Tokyo reported 239 measles cases, the second-highest figure since record-keeping began in 2008 (1,174 cases that year). Measles is highly contagious and airborne; vaccination remains the most effective prevention. Outside the regular schedule (which includes 1-year-olds and the year before elementary school), vaccination is self-funded, costing at least 10,000 yen. About 26 million yen is allocated from this year's contingency budget. Governor Koike urged residents to consider vaccination to protect themselves and others.

articles.summary: Tokyo will begin free emergency measles vaccination on May 18 at eight designated infectious disease medical institutions to curb a rapidly spreading outbreak. Eligible residents are those with no prior measles history who have had contact with a measles patient within 72 hours and whose vaccination history is either zero or one dose; eligibility is determined by public health centers. The measles virus is highly contagious, and vaccination within 72 hours of exposure is considered preventive against illness. articles.summary: Tokyo will launch an emergency measles vaccination program for close contacts of measles patients within 72 hours of exposure, starting May 18, 2026, in response to a surge in measles cases. The MR vaccine (measles-rubella) will be provided free of charge with the recipient’s consent, funded from contingency funds (~26 million yen). The target is primarily Tokyo residents. After a measles case is confirmed, public health centers trace the patient’s movements and identify contacts, typically household members. Among these, individuals who are unvaccinated, have only one prior dose, or have unknown vaccination status are eligible. Centers will contact eligible persons and administer MR vaccination upon consent. Initially eight designated infectious disease medical institutions in Tokyo will offer vaccination, with plans to expand to about 25 sites.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infection confirmed in Kitakyushu City for the first time in six years; possible exposure to a large number of people.
articles.summary: As of May 15, 2026, Kitakyushu City confirms a measles infection—the first in six years—in a woman in her 30s from Wakamatsu Ward, with potential exposure to a large number of people. The patient developed fever on May 7 and a generalized rash, with laboratory confirmation on May 14. She is reported to have visited the Wakamatsu Ward Office and supermarkets between May 7–13. The city notes over 400 measles infections since January, nearing the ten-year high, with no confirmed cases in the city since 2020. No details on infection source or vaccination status are provided. This case highlights ongoing measles transmission risk in urban settings and the need for continued surveillance and public health measures to limit exposure in public spaces.

articles.summary: Measles exposure alert in Shizuoka City after an individual living outside Shizuoka Prefecture was confirmed with measles. The patient visited the Shin-Tōmei Expressway, Shimizu Parking Area, in Shimizu Ward, Shizuoka City on May 6 during the contagious period, staying from 12:15 p.m. to around 1:30 p.m. while en route by private car to another prefecture; no other city facilities were used. The city cautions people who used the Shimizu Parking Area during that window, or anyone with measles symptoms, to contact healthcare providers in advance about potential exposure before seeking care. The measles virus is reported to survive in air for less than two hours, and there is currently no infection risk from having used the Shimizu Parking Area.

articles.headlineTranslated: Adults should be vigilant for measles and mumps; severe cases can cause encephalitis and infertility, lifelong hearing loss... risk of long-term sequelae: Kii Minpo AGARA | Wakayama Prefecture's news site
articles.summary: As of May 14, 2026, Japan reports nationwide measles outbreaks, with adults at risk of severe disease—pneumonia, encephalitis, and rare long-term complications such as subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Separately, mumps outbreaks emerge in April–May as children enter new environments. Dr. Yoshihiro Atsumi of Clinic For emphasizes high infectiousness in crowded, poorly ventilated spaces and notes an 'immune-desert generation' (30s–50s) with unknown vaccination histories. The rise partly reflects inbound travelers introducing viruses. For measles, additional vaccination may be considered if immunity is uncertain; testing for immunity is possible but not mandatory. For mumps, vaccination remains voluntary in Japan; complications include orchitis in males, oophoritis in females, and mumps-related deafness, estimated at over 100 cases annually in Japan. Prevention centers on vaccination, avoiding dense gatherings, and contacting medical services by phone or telemedicine when symptoms appear.

articles.summary: Measles infections are rising nationwide in 2026, with adults at risk of severe disease including pneumonia, encephalitis, and rare late-onset neurologic sequelae such as subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Measles spreads by airborne transmission, especially in crowded indoor settings; inbound travelers contribute introductions. An 'immune gap generation' (roughly ages 30–50) may have only one MMR dose or grown up before routine vaccination. Immunity testing is available, but those with unknown history may receive an extra MMR dose; three doses pose no known extra risk. Separately, mumps risks in adults include orchitis in males and possible infertility, and less commonly oophoritis in females; mumps-related deafness is lifelong, estimated at a low rate, with Japan reporting over 100 cases annually. MMR vaccination in Japan is voluntary. Prevention centers on vaccination, avoiding crowded environments, and seeking medical advice (telemedicine encouraged) when symptoms appear.

articles.headlineTranslated: Ten times more contagious than the flu! Be on alert for measles; I, diagnosed with a “cold,” wandered to the brink of death | JBpress
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Japan is accelerating. Cumulative cases rose from 197 on April 1 to 436 by April 30, with Tokyo reporting 211 cases, followed by Kanagawa 40, Kagoshima 34, Chiba 27, Saitama 26, and Aichi 25. Measles’ basic reproduction number is 12–18, about ten times that of influenza, and it spreads via airborne transmission, yielding infection rates exceeding 90% for unvaccinated individuals in the same room; even entering a room after the patient has left can transmit. The author recalls a near-fatal measles experience in his 20s, highlighting a typical progression: a 10–12 day incubation, fever for 2–4 days, then widespread red rash and high fever (>39°C). Vaccination gaps shape current risk: people born after 2000-04 are expected to have two doses; those born 1972-10-01 to 2000-04-01 may have only one; those born before 1972 had no routine vaccination, leaving them vulnerable. The outbreak predominantly affects people in their 20s–30s.

articles.summary: As of May 12, 2026, Fukui Prefecture reported a measles infection in a man in his 40s, who recovered at home. He had traveled to Vietnam in late April, with infection thought most probable there. Fever began May 6; he sought care May 8; rash appeared May 10; measles virus was confirmed May 11. He returned to Fukui by private car from Kanagawa on May 6 and has since avoided public transport. Authorities advised suspected cases to contact medical facilities before visiting and to avoid public transit. Measles virus can survive in air for under two hours; typical progression includes fever and cold-like symptoms about 10 days after exposure, followed by high fever and a widespread rash with Koplik spots in the mouth. Nationally, 436 measles cases had been reported as of April 26.
